Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires and the players have made their way out in the middle. Usman Ghani and Rahmanullah Gurbaz will open with their blades for Afghanistan. Naseem Shah comes to bowl. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, Pakistan managed to put up a total of 130 runs and they will look to defend it. For Afghanistan, the onus is on their batters to put up a gritty stand and chase this down. Can they win the series? Or will Pakistan manage to level it? Let's find out together. Chase coming up shortly...

Afghanistan were excellent with the ball! It was Fazalhaq Farooqi who ran a havoc over the batters at the start and he got support from the rest of their bowlers. He chipped in with two wickets while Karim Janat, Rashid Khan, and Naveen-ul-Haq had one in their bank. They will be happy with their performance and will be hoping to win this series.

Well, the struggle with the bat continues for Pakistan. They were under the pump from the word go. They lost two wickets in the very first over. Imad Wasim was the only batter who stood for them, but the non-strikers kept on losing wickets at regular intervals. They moved the gear up at the very end and made their side reach a par total of 130 runs.

OUT! RUN OUT! Shadab Khan is run out off the last delivery but Pakistan have managed to get 130 on the board. This one is bowled full and outside off. Khan steers it to backward point and tries to steal a second run. However, the throw is pretty good from Usman Ghani and Rahmanullah Gurbaz whips the bails off as Shadab Khan fails to make his ground even with a big dive.

OUT! LBW! Fazalhaq Farooqi gets two in two and Fazalhaq Farooqi is on a hat-trick! Abdullah Shafique becomes the first player in T20I cricket to get four ducks in a row. This is beautifully bowled, a fullish delivery shaping into middle and leg. Abdullah Shafique tries to flick it but misses. The ball hits his pads and after a big appeal, the umpire raises his finger. Abdullah Shafique takes the DRS though but the UltraEdge shows no bat and the Ball Tracking ends up showing three reds. So, the original decision stays and Pakistan is rocked early.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Rahmanullah Gurbaz with a stunner and Afghanistan have got an early breakthrough! Lands it on a good length, around off. The ball nips away a bit after coming in with the angle and Saim Ayub who tries to defend the ball gets an outside edge. The ball goes left of the keeper and Gurbaz takes a brilliant catch diving to his left. Fazalhaq Farooqi is pumped up!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the anthems now and are all set to get the action underway in few minutes time. Afghanistan players are out there in the middle. Saim Ayub and Mohammad Haris are the openers for Pakistan. Fazalhaq Farooqi to start the proceedings with the ball. Here we go...

We are ready for the national anthems now. First up it will be Pakistan's anthem followed by the Afghanistan one. It is a must-win game for Pakistan and we can expect a better performance from them in this game.

Rashid Khan, the skipper of Afghanistan says that they wanted to bowl first. Mentions that Sharjah pitch sometimes look different and behaves differently. Adds that they just want to enjoy their game and the important thing is to adjust to the conditions. Informs that they have one change with Gulbadin Naib missing out and Usman Ghani back in the side.

Shadab Khan, the skipper of Pakistan says that they will bat first. Tells that it is a typical Sharjah pitch and in the last game it was different. Mentions that they are looking forward to this game as the four debutants were bit nervous in the last game. Informs that they have one change with Mohammad Nawaz coming in. Talks about Ihsanullah and says that he has shown his talent in PSL and they are excited about him.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Usman Ghani (In place of Gulbadin Naib), Najibullah Zadran, Mohammad Nabi, Karim Janat, Azmatullah Omarzai, Rashid Khan (C), Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Fazalhaq Farooqi, Naveen-ul-Haq.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Mohammad Haris, Saim Ayub, Abdullah Shafique, Tayyab Tahir, Azam Khan (WK), Shadab Khan (C), Imad Wasim, Mohammad Nawaz (In place of Faheem Ashraf), Naseem Shah, Zaman Khan, Ihsanullah.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and will BAT first.

Pakistan, on the other hand, could not show any application with the bat on a difficult pitch. They would be hoping for a better performance in this game. Pakistan does have a young team, and it is a good opportunity for youngsters to show their potential when their team is under pressure. Can they level the series? Or will Rashid Khan and his boys seal the series? Let's find out. Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Hello and a warm welcome to the second T20I of this three-match T20I series between Pakistan and Afghanistan. The first game turned out to be in the favor of Afghanistan, as their bowlers put up a great show to restrict Pakistan to a below-par total. Their batters did a good job of chasing it with ease and getting a lead in the series. They would be high on confidence and would look to seal this series now.
... MATCH DAY ...

After a convincing victory in the first T20I of this three-match series, Afghanistan would be looking to put up a show similar to the first game. Afghanistan won the first match quite comfortably as the inexperienced squad of Pakistan could not handle the lethal bowling attack of Afghanistan. The hosts could only manage to post a total of 92 runs after their quota of overs. Rashid Khan was fantastic with his bowling changes and field settings and looked better prepared to lead the unit than before. Pakistan, on the contrary, were poor with the bat as no player stood up to take responsibility in the absence of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan. However, Pakistan's bowling was impressive and troubled the Afghan batters even in such a low-scoring affair, the flop show with the bat haunted them. Afghanistan would be stepping into this game looking to seal the series and win the first-ever bilateral T20I series between the two nations whereas Pakistan would want to bounce back and prove that their bench strength is capable of delivering the goods. With both sides looking for a performance of significance, this game promises to be a thriller. Expect a fiercely contested battle on a surface which could again favour the bowlers.
